items.summary: चुनाव आयोग ने दिल्ली में जारी विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (एसआईआर) के बाद ड्राफ्ट वोटर लिस्ट जारी की. जिसमें करीब 47 लाख लोगों के नाम हटा दिए गए हैं. इनमें से बुराड़ी विधानसभा क्षेत्र में करीब 1 लाख 67 हजार लोगों के नाम शामिल हैं. बुराड़ी दिल्ली के उत्तरी हिस्से में आता है. यहां कई उद्योग हैं और बड़ी संख्या में प्रवासी मजदूर काम यहां करते हैं. इनमें कई लोग ऐसे हैं जो पहले भी उसी पते पर वोट देते रहे हैं लेकिन इस बार ड्राफ्ट लिस्ट में उनका नाम नहीं है. ड्राफ्ट सूची में नाम ना आने से लोग परेशान हैं. कुछ लोगों को चिंता है कि अगर उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट में नहीं होगा तो उन्हें सरकारी योजनाओं का लाभ लेने में भी दिक्कत हो सकती है. इसी परेशानी के बीच कई लोग अपना नाम ठीक करवाने के लिए चुनाव आयोग के अधिकारियों के पास दफ्तर में लंबी कतारों में खड़े नजर आए. एसआईआर की प्रक्रिया ने न सिर्फ आम लोगों बल्कि बूथ लेवल अधिकारियों को भी परेशान किया है. खासकर बुराड़ी जैसे इलाके में जहां बड़ी संख्या में प्रवासी मजदूर रहते हैं और काम की वजह से एक जगह से दूसरी जगह शिफ्ट होते रहते हैं. देखिए हमारी ये खास रिपोर्ट. जिस सीट पर केजरीवाल मामूली अंतर से हारे, वहां 2025 चुनाव से पहले जुड़े 40 फीसदी नाम एसआईआर के ड्राफ्ट में गायब एसआईआर का पहला ड्राफ्ट, 40% का पत्ता साफ: तुगलकाबाद, ओखला, आरके पुरम, जंगपुरा और बदरपुर सर्वाधिक प्रभावित

items.title: Long queues, voters in limbo: In Delhi seat with largest SIR deletions
items.summary: After the Special Intensive Revision in Delhi, nearly 47 lakh names have been temporarily left out of the draft electoral roll. In Burari alone, around 1.67 lakh names are missing, making it the largest exclusions in terms of absolute numbers across the capital. Located in north Delhi, Burari has several industrial areas and is home to a large migrant workforce, including workers from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Many say they have voted from the same addresses in previous elections, but have now found their names missing. The deletions have left residents worried and scrambling to get their names restored. At the AERO office, long queues formed as voters sought corrections. Burari resident Avinash, who believed there was an error in his voter registration, so he used ChatGPT to fill out Form 8 to correct his details but still received a notice. The SIR exercise has also put pressure on Booth Level Officers, particularly in areas like Burari where migrant workers frequently move for work. For residents, the concern goes beyond voting: some fear that being left off the electoral roll could also create difficulties in accessing government welfare schemes. A quarter-century of Modi governance calls for questions and a hamper. To mark the occasion, we have offers for subscribers and other readers .

items.title: Gujarat HC rejects Ravi Nair’s plea for interim release in Adani defamation case
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court has rejected journalist Ravi Nair’s plea for interim release in a criminal defamation case filed against him by the Adani Group, Bar and Bench reported. The court had earlier given Adani Enterprises additional time to respond to Nair’s petition challenging his custody in a criminal defamation case, pushing the matter to September 23. Justice MK Thakker on Wednesday reserved her decision on Nair’s petition. The court said that it will dictate the order next Wednesday. Nair, a contributor to adaniwatch.org , was convicted of defamation by a Judicial Magistrate First Class in Gandhinagar in February over a series of tweets and articles accusing the Adani Group of corruption, crony capitalism and misuse of government agencies. He was sentenced to a year’s simple imprisonment and fined Rs 5,000. The Sessions Court later suspended his sentence and released him on bail while he appealed the conviction, on conditions including regular court appearances and surrendering his passport. According to a Bar and Bench report, Nair was taken back into custody last week after a non-bailable warrant was issued against him. The Indian Express reported that a September 3 Sessions Court order first held that Nair was missing and deliberately avoiding arrest; a subsequent September 17 order rejected his bid to cancel the warrant and directed that he be sent to jail. He then moved the High Court for release. At Monday’s hearing before Justice M K Thakker, senior counsel Mitesh Amin, appearing for Adani Enterprises, sought a short adjournment to place “certain legal and factual aspects” on record, according to The Indian Express . Nair’s counsel, Advocate Abhik Chimni, opposed the request and pushed for interim relief, arguing that the case was already at the appellate stage and that a Supreme Court ruling supported his client's position. As Bar and Bench reported , Chimni argued in court, “Why should I even spend one day in jail?” The court granted Adani’s adjournment but made clear it would not allow any further delay. Adani Enterprises filed a defamation case in September 2021, alleging that tweets posted by Nair between October 2020 and July 2021 about the Adani Group had falsely damaged its reputation among investors and regulators. Nair maintains that his posts amounted to fair, public-interest journalism based on information publicly available. A quarter-century of Modi governance calls for questions and a hamper. items.title: ‘Found out after video went viral’: Father of Jamui assault survivor says ‘arrest is not enough’
items.summary: “I will be happy only when my daughter gets justice. I hope they are encountered by police. Arrest is not enough,” said the father of the minor who was harassed and assaulted by a group of men in Bihar’s Jamui district on September 19. A key accused in the case, Nandan Yadav, was shot in the leg by the police on September 22 and arrested, taking the total number of arrests to six. According to The Times of India , three of the accused are adults, while the other three are minors. Videos of the assault, which showed the girl and a male friend, both of them class 10 students, being surrounded, chased, and harassed for roughly an hour, went viral on social media, prompting outrage and the police investigation. Jamui is the Lok Sabha constituency under which Tarapur, the assembly seat represented by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, falls and Opposition leaders have raised serious concerns about the state of law and order there. Jamui Police have also identified 120 URLs carrying the video and say they are taking steps to stop its circulation. What happened on September 19 At around 5 pm on September 19, the girl left her home in Jamui for her tuition class, expecting to return after her evening lessons. Instead, according to her father, she and her friend went out for ice cream during a break between classes, where some men on two bikes allegedly began disturbing her and behaving inappropriately. “My daughter is quite disturbed after this incident. She told us about it a day after it happened when the video started going viral on the internet,” her father told Newslaundry . The girl and her male friend were allegedly stopped by the group, surrounded and subjected to harassment for around an hour, making repeated attempts to escape. Yadav allegedly chased and grabbed the girl from behind, later lifting her onto his lap; her friend intervened and freed her, leading to a scuffle, though the accused continued trying to stop the two from leaving. The videos, which surfaced on social media soon after, prompted Jamui Police to take cognisance and begin an investigation. According to Jamui Superintendent of Police Vishwajeet Dayal, Yadav, 25, is now in police custody, with more arrests likely once police complete his interrogation. “After we interrogate Yadav, more people will be identified,” said Dayal. items.title: SFI moves Delhi High Court over suspension of Instagram account
items.summary: Student’s Federation of India (SFI) has approached the Delhi High Court challenging the alleged delay by the Central government’s grievance appellate committee (GAC) in deciding its appeal against Instagram’s permanent disabling of one its accounts. Justice Amit Mahajan is scheduled to hear the case on September 24. SFI is the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). According to SFI’s plea, Instagram permanently disabled the SFI Delhi account on July 5, stating that it “may be associated with another account that has gone against our rules” and therefore did not comply with its community standards on account integrity. SFI states that Instagram did not disclose any further particulars or identify the allegedly associated account. The account, created in 2018, had around 13,000 followers. The petitioners said they first appealed the disabling on July 7 and subsequently approached Meta's grievance officer on July 9. However, they received no response, following which they approached the GAC on August 12. As of September 16, the GAC website showed the appeal as “under process”, despite more than 30 days having elapsed, the petition stated. The petitioner has relied on Rule 3A(4) of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 requires the GAC to deal with appeals expeditiously and endeavour to resolve them finally within 30 calendar days. It has also sought a direction to the GAC to conduct its appeal process in conformity with the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed under Articles 14, 19(1)(a), 19(1)(g), and 21. The petition was filed through advocate Naman Kumar.

items.title: Punjab & Haryana HC seeks explanation from judge for wrongly attributing district court order to High Court
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently sought an explanation from an additional district judge for mistakenly writing that the High Court had stayed proceedings in an application moved by Punjab State Warehousing Corporation for execution of an arbitration award [Hardev Singh and Ors v Punjab State Warehousing Corporation and Anr] The Court was informed that the order staying the operation of the award was actually passed by an additional district judge in Chandigarh who is hearing a challenge against the award. Justice Lapita Banerji called it a serious issue and sought a report from the district judge of Muktsar Sahib. "Let a status report be called from the learned District Judge, Sri Muktsar Sahib, explaining the anomaly that has crept into the order dated August 19, 2026, passed in EXE-86-2024. It is also to be explained how despite recording that the presence of the decree holder is awaited the appearance of the learned counsel for the decree holder is recorded and how after recording that the JDs No. 1 to 7 are proceeded against “ex parte”, the learned ADJ recorded the presence of the learned counsel for JDs No.3 to 6," the Court said. Justice Lapita Banerji The matter pertains to a domestic arbitration award won by Punjab State Warehousing Corporation against an industrial unit over the short supply of rice in return for the paddy entrusted to it. In the execution proceedings filed by the Corporation, the additional district judge at Muktsar Sahab on March 27 issued warrants of attachment of property of judgment debtors in the proceedings. The same was challenged by the judgment debtors before the High Court. During a hearing of the revision petition on September 16, Punjab State Warehousing Corporation's Standing Counsel Abhilaksh Gaind told the Court that the additional district judge on August 19 stayed the execution proceedings after relying upon a High Court stay order that didn't exist. However, senior counsel representing the judgment debtors submitted that the additional district judge had only wrongly recorded that the High Court had passed the stay order when the stay order was in fact passed by a Chandigarh district court judge while hearing their objection petition. Therefore, the Court proceeded to seek an explanation from the judge. Senior Advocate Vijay Kumar Jindal with Advocates Ajay Pal Singh, Abhishek Shukla and Vijayveer represented the petitioners. items.title: Did Odisha know of CBI request to question IPS officer when it forwarded his name for DGP post? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked whether the Odisha government was aware of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)'s request to question senior IPS officer Susanta Kumar Nath when it included his name in the panel of officers for appointment as Director General of Police (DGP). A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana raised the question while hearing a petition against Nath's exclusion from the race due to an ongoing CBI probe into the sub-inspector (SI) recruitment scam. The State has withdrawn the integrity certificate issued to Nath for consideration for the DGP post in view of the CBI's request and is now sending a fresh list of IPS officers to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) as part of the DGP appointment process. Today, Justice Bagchi asked whether the State should not have informed the CBI beforehand about the pending CBI probe. "We are not saying the integrity certificate should be withdrawn. We are not clear on that. But what we are asking is: if the FIR has already been registered, it refers to a certain role and names the person as an accused, then is it not the duty of the State Government to place this before the Commission?" the judge asked. While giving an example of a police officer accused in an FIR over use of pellet guns against protesters, Justice Bagchi asked, "Should the UPSC be kept in the dark about this FIR?" items.title: Kerala High Court grants bail to school teacher arrested in Vadakara drug trafficking case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday granted bail to a school teacher arrested in connection with a drug trafficking case registered by the Vadakara police [Kavya K v State of Kerala]. Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the bail application of 29-year-old Kavya K, who is the third accused in the case. While granting bail, the Court took into account Kavya's judicial custody since July 25. " The applicant was remanded to judicial custody on 25.07.2026. The investigation is almost over. The recovery has been effected. The applicant has no criminal antecedents. For these reasons, I do not find any reason to hold that the continued detention of the applicant is required for any purpose. Hence, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail, " the Court said. Justice Kauser Edappagath The bail plea was filed in connection with the crime registered by the Vadakara Police. Kavya was booked under Section 22(b) and Section 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS Act), for offences relating to possession of psychotropic substances and criminal conspiracy. According to the prosecution, Kavya and the other accused had allegedly conspired to transport and sell narcotics drugs. Police found one of the accused in possession of 2.108 grams of MDMA (commonly known as ecstasy, a synthetic drug) and alleged that financial transactions connected with the offence were carried out through Kavya's bank account and that of another accused. Kavya subsequently moved before the High Court seeking bail and argued that she had been falsely implicated in the case. She stated that was no material connecting her to the alleged crime. The prosecution opposed the plea, maintaining that the transactions were part of her intentional criminal acts. The Court, however, ordered her release after noting that the investigation was almost complete and that she had no criminal antecedents. It granted her bail subject to several conditions, including executing ₹1 lakh bond with two solvent sureties and appearing before the investigating officer every Saturday until further orders. Kavya was also directed to cooperate with the investigation, refrain from contacting witnesses or tramping with evidence. She was also ordered not to leave Kerala without the trial court's permission. Advocates MP Priyeshkumar, OT Jabish and Divya TP represented Kavya. Public prosecutor Thomas Sabu Vadakekut appeared for the state. [Read Order]

items.title: My learned friend, there's AI in the room
items.summary: Christopher Nolan worked with physicist Kip Thorne on Interstellar. Yet, he has said he does not use a smartphone. The man explores black holes; I am still trying to escape my WhatsApp groups. For me, the lesson is not to reject technology. It is to protect the mind that uses it. A director can embrace extraordinary filmmaking technology without making himself available to every notification. A lawyer should be permitted the same ambition. Ask a lawyer a difficult legal question and you will usually receive an argument. Ask for their screen-time report and you may receive an application for adjournment. I include myself in the second category. This is not a sermon from someone who has achieved enlightenment by switching to a basic phone. Learn to use AI well and learn when to leave technology alone. Be ready for change without making everyone else pass a compulsory examination in enthusiasm. My first search engine had shelves During my years working with the late Shanti Bhushan, I was told to put my laptop away and look at his library. Read the books. Understand the principles. Work through the problem. For six years, my search engine had shelves. When I suggested finding judgments online, his point, as I understood it, was that those judgments answered questions already adjudicated. Our work also required us to interpret and develop the law, sometimes where an answer was not already waiting. That was not permission to disregard precedent. It was an instruction not to mistake finding a precedent for having an argument. There is a difference between asking which judgment supports the result we want and asking why the law should produce that result. Research must serve the reasoning, not conceal its absence. I would not require a junior today to reproduce those years of research in exactly the same way. The lesson worth preserving is intellectual independence. Nostalgia is not a training programme As a first-generation litigating lawyer, I welcome the help AI offers with research, document review and initial drafting. A young lawyer with limited support can get a foothold in unfamiliar material. There is nothing noble about spending an afternoon rearranging paragraphs rather than understanding why the argument fails. I would encourage juniors to ask AI to challenge their position, identify an overlooked question or suggest a counterargument. Then investigate the response. items.title: Why ESMA not invoked against striking bus drivers? Delhi High Court asks government, DTC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday questioned the Delhi government and the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) about why the provisions of the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) have not been invoked against DTC drivers who have been on strike for the past several days [Ami Sisodia vs Government of NCT of Delhi & Ors ]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia made the remark while hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition raising concerns over the disruption caused by the protests . Advocate Avneesh Ahlawat appeared for DTC and told the Bench that there is no union of the DTC drivers and that persons involved are sending WhatsApp messages calling for the strike and vandalising the buses. She stated that steps have been taken by the DTC to address the situation and nearly 96% of the buses are now back in service. Ahlawat stated that the DTC had sent a file to the Delhi government for invoking ESMA. The Court then disposed of the PIL while asking the government to take a decision on invoking ESMA. "We expect the state will review and take a decision as per law to ensure that the plying of DTC buses is maintained on the roads," the Court ordered. It added that if the situation does not improve, the petitioner can approach the High Court again. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia Bus drivers, conductors and other personnel associated with the operation of public buses have been on strike since September 15 demanding an increase in their wages and other benefits. The PIL is seeking directions for urgent restoration, maintenance and continuity of public bus transport services in Delhi. The petitioner Ami Sisodia stated that due to the unavailability of free public transport provided for women, she has to resort to taking expensive alternate modes of transport to commute. The plea said that the strike was impacting lakhs of residents, students, daily-wage workers, salaried employees, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, patients and economically weaker commuters who depend upon affordable public transportation. Further, it was contended that the strike shifted the pressure of commuters on the Delhi Metro services. The petition was filed through advocate Vikrant Dabas.

items.title: National security trumps personal rights: Karnataka High Court upholds land acquisition for DRDO
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently observed that the interests of national security must take precedence over personal rights, while restoring the acquistion of land for a Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) AI/ robotics centre [ Defence Research and Development Organisation v. Special Land Acquisition Officer ] . A Division Bench comprising Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan on September 21 set aside a 2014 single-judge Bench ruling that had earlier quashed the land acquisition proceedings. The single-judge had reasoned that objections raised by the original landowners had not been properly considered by the relevant authorities during the land acquisition proceedings. The DRDO and the Union government had challenged this ruling by way of appeals, which have now been allowed by the High Court's Division Bench. The Division Bench found that the original landowners’ objections had, in fact, been properly considered and that they failed to show any real prejudice. Notably, the Court also highlighted that the acquired land would be used for research into defence measures. In such matters, national interest takes precedence over personal rights, it said. "National security is paramount and must always take precedence over individual interests or personal rights. While personal rights are undoubtedly precious, they cannot be asserted in a manner that compromises the safety and security of the nation. The nation must come first, for the protection of the country is the foundation upon which all individual rights and freedoms securely rest," the ruling stated. Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan The Court further underscored that institutions such as the DRDO work tirelessly to safeguard the nation and strengthen its security, through research, innovation and the development of advanced defence systems. "In the modern era, when the nation faces increasingly sophisticated threats in the fields of cyber warfare, artificial intelligence and advanced technology, the research and functioning of the (DRDO) Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (‘CAIR’) assume vital importance. Its continued research and technological advancement are essential to strengthening the nation’s defence preparedness, protecting critical systems and safeguarding the sovereignty, security and integrity of the country," it added. items.title: Five Karnataka auto, taxi driver bodies move Supreme Court against HC verdict permitting bike taxis
items.summary: Five auto and taxi driver associations in Karnataka have moved the Supreme Court against a Karnataka High Court verdict permitting bike taxis in the State. They have challenged the January 23 judgment directing the State to consider applications for registering motorcycles as transport vehicles and granting permits to operate them as contract carriages. The petition has also been filed by an individual driver, Sathish KS. The five associations are Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Auto Chalakara Sanghatane, Karnataka Venkategowda Auto Mathu Taxi Chalakara Sangha, Greater Bangalore Chalakara Sangha, Karnataka Sarathigala Mahasangha and Jai Karnataka Sarathi Sene Trust. An individual driver, Sathish KS, has also filed a separate petition. According to their plea, the High Court effectively created a regulatory pathway for bike taxis in a field that falls within the domain of the State government and statutory transport authorities A constitutional court cannot compel the State to create or implement a particular transport policy to suit the business interests of aggregators, the plea has contended. A key ground in the plea concerns the impact on existing auto-rickshaw and taxi operators. As per the plea, around 1.5 lakh auto-rickshaw drivers, taxi permit holders and other regulated operators in Bengaluru could be affected if bike taxis are permitted without a comparable regulatory framework. Such operators are already subject to permit conditions, fitness norms, insurance requirements, taxation, fare regulation and licensing requirements. Allowing a competing category without similar safeguards, they argue, would raise concerns over regulatory parity, it has been contended. The plea also relies on a 2019 expert committee report that was against permitting bike taxis in Bengaluru on grounds including road safety, congestion, road-space efficiency and emissions. The Government of Karnataka has also filed an appeal against the order of the High Court. The plea is yet to be heard at length. The petition was filed through advocate K Shiva.

items.title: LoP reduced to ornamental role in selection of Election Commissioners: Justice Dipankar Datta in split verdict
items.summary: Justice Dipankar Datta of the Supreme Court on Wednesday said that the Leader of Opposition's (LoP) role in the selection of Election Commissioners of the Election Commission of India (ECI) is only ornamental as the Union government holds an overwhelming majority in the selection panel. Justice Datta made the observations in his separate opinion on petitions challenging the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. The 2023 Act is primarily under challenge before the top court for replacing the Chief Justice of India (CJI) with a cabinet minister on the selection panel. The panel at present comprises the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister. Justice Datta in his prima facie view said that it was highly unlikely that the cabinet minister would ever disagree with the Prime Minister. The judge stressed that it was not enough for the ECI to be independent but it must also appear to be independent. "The Minister nominated by the Prime Minister to function as the third member of the selection committee, chaired by the Prime Minister, cannot be expected to defy his own nominator and risk his continuation as such nominated member on the committee for all practical purposes. Even otherwise, the collective responsibility doctrine would preclude the Minister to oppose his Prime Minister," Justice Datta said. He further opined that it is far-fetched to expect that a minister, who is part of the Council of Ministers and bound by the collective responsibility under Article 75(3), would take a stand contrary to the Prime Minister in the matter of appointment to a sensitive constitutional office. "In such a circumstance, the inclusion of a Cabinet Minister in the selection committee fails to provide the independent counterweight that a neutral selector could, and the Cabinet Minister would merely echo the voice of his leader, and consequently, the presence of the Leader of opposition in the selection committee becomes largely ornamental, without furthering the purpose of his inclusion," he added. items.title: DHCBA objects to Central Motor Vehicles Rules amendments on traffic challans
items.summary: The Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) has voiced deep concern and strong objection to the recent amendments made to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 governing the adjudication of traffic challans. In a resolution passed on Wednesday, association's executive committee called on the concerned authorities to reconsider the changes, emphasising that disputed traffic challans must remain subject to effective, independent and accessible judicial scrutiny. Therefore, the bar body objected to the changes as per which contested challans are now required to be initially adjudicated by executive or departmental authorities rather than an independent judicial forum. "Disputed questions concerning the facts, evidence and liability arising from a challan ought to be adjudicated by an independent judicial forum only," the resolution stated. The DHCBA further flagged the requirement mandating a pre-deposit of 50 percent of the challan amount before approaching a competent court. This is a substantial financial impediment that curbs access to judicial remedies, particularly for ordinary citizens, the DHCBA said. Additionally, the bar body took exception to the provision that deems a challan accepted if it is not contested within a 45-day window. It noted that this mechanism is unreasonable and will adversely impact individuals facing digital accessibility hurdles or difficulties understanding complex online procedures. "The Executive Committee recognises the need for expeditious traffic enforcement, however, the same cannot come at the cost of fair adjudication and meaningful access to justice," the resolution emphasised. The resolution was signed by DHCBA President N Hariharan and Secretary Vikram Singh Panwar. [Read Resolution]

items.title: Judges appointing judges is a myth: Justice Dipankar Datta pulls up government for selectively clearing Collegium proposals
items.summary: Justice Dipankar Datta of the Supreme Court on Wednesday said that it was wrong to claim that judges appoint judges in the country, and critcised the government for selectively clearing Collegium proposals for the appointment of judges. Justice Datta made the observation while addressing a submission made by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta during the hearing of petitions challenging a 2023 law that gave more say to the Executive in the selection of members of the Election Commission of India (ECI). The petitions raised concerns about the government Executive's dominance in the selection panel that appoints ECI members. One of the arguments raised by the Central government to counter this concern was that even in judicial appointments, existing judges have a predominant say in the appointment of future judges under the existing Collegium system. In a ruling pronounced today, Justice Datta took exception to this argument. He underscored that even under the Collegium system, there is a consultative process at play between the government and the judiciary before judges are appointed. items.title: Bombay High Court orders total ban on firecrackers on streets, laser lights during festivals
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has issued directives to curb severe noise and air pollution during festive processions across Maharashtra [In Re: Noise and Environmental Pollution] By way of an order passed on September 22, a division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale ordered a complete ban on bursting firecrackers on public streets and roads during festivities. Further, laser lights, high-intensity lumen lights and beams have also been completely prohibited during celebrations. The Court also imposed a slew of obligations on organisers of such festivities/ celebrations. They have to instal internal sound limiters and decibel meters at festival venues and processions and must also submit security deposits of ₹1 lakh. The Court passed the order in a suo motu public interest litigation petition initiated by it to address unchecked pollution during festivals like Ganeshotsav. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale During the hearing, the Court had orally remarked that celebrations are not meant for people to die or suffer health-wise. The bench emphasised that enforcement must be preventive rather than relying on minor fines after the damage to citizens' health is already done. To implement these preventive measures, the Court issued several key directives: The Court ordered a total ban on bursting firecrackers on public streets and roads during festivities. Laser lights, high-intensity lumen lights, and beams are completely prohibited during celebrations. Organizers must install visible decibel measurement meters at venues and processions.They must also furnish affidavits guaranteeing sound systems contain internal limiters. Organisers must submit security deposits of ₹1 lakh for groups or ₹50,000 for individuals. Deposits stand forfeited upon any decibel violation. Authorities must immediately seize and confiscate non-compliant sound systems and offending instruments. Designated officials must actively measure and record decibel levels in the presence of organizer representatives. Processions must publicly display written permissions alongside the names, addresses, and mobile numbers of responsible organizers. Authorities must evaluate the cumulative noise impact in a ward before issuing multiple permits. The Court also ordered officials to sensitise organisers about their legal obligations when processions begin. The 2023 Act is under challenge for replacing the Chief Justice of India (CJI) with a Cabinet Minister on the selection panel which appoints Election Commissioners. The Central government had requested the Court to refer the matter to a larger bench under Article 145(3) of the Constitution. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma had reserved its decision on the demand for reference on July 30. Justice Datta rejected the government's request for reference. He went on to deliver a prima facie opinion on the challenge to the 2023 Act. "We heard these petitions for over 5 days, speaking in one voice would have served the voice of institutional cohesion. items.title: KSLU tells Karnataka High Court it has introduced 1% reservation for transgender law students
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday took note of Karnataka State Law University's (KSLU) decision to provide 1% horizontal reservation for transgender persons and to relax the eligibility criteria to 40% marks for admission to its three-year LL.B courses. A Division Bench of Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice TP Vivekananda was informed of the development. Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice T P Vivekananda The case arose from a plea filed by transgender candidate Mugil Anbu Vasantha challenging the admission policy of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) Bangalore. On December 16, 2024, the High Court partly allowed the plea, holding that NLSIU's existing admission and financial aid policies did not adequately ensure equality of opportunity for transgender persons. The Court had then directed NLSIU to formulate a transgender reservation and financial aid policy before commencement of the next academic year's admission process. In the interim, NLSIU was directed to provide 0.5% reservation along with fee waiver for transgender candidates. NLSIU subsequently challenged the order in appeal. Counsel appearing for KSLU on Monday placed on record an admission notification dated September 16 and submitted that it specifically provides for 1% reservation for transgender persons and lowering of the eligibility criteria to 40% marks for the three-year LL.B. course. It was submitted that these provisions were incorporated pursuant to a special government order dated September 15. Vasantha, who appeared in person, submitted that the last date for submission of applications was the following day and, therefore, eligible transgender candidates would not have sufficient time to submit their applications under the newly notified reservation provision. The Additional Advocate General, along with counsel for KSLU, submitted that the reservation could only be implemented as horizontal reservation in accordance with law. The Court noted that the government order specifically provided that the inclusion of the reservation in the admission notification would be subject to further orders of the Court and guidelines to be framed in the matter. The Bench further said that the present proceedings arose from an appeal preferred by NLSIU, in which an interim direction had already been issued to keep one seat reserved for the first respondent Mugil Anbu Vasantha. items.title: Subhash Chandra moves NCLAT against NCLT stay on alienation of assets in ₹6.5 crore repayment plan case
items.summary: Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra has moved the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) against a September 1 order of a five-member special bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) restraining him from alienating his assets. A Bench of Officiating Chairperson Justice (retd) Yogesh Khanna and Technical Members Barun Mitra and Ajai Das Mehrotra took up the appeal and directed Chandra to serve copies of the plea on the creditors. It then posted the matter for hearing on September 29. Senior Advocate Dhurv Mehta, appearing for Chandra, told the NCLAT that the appeal challenges the order passed by a special bench of NCLT on September 1. Several creditors, however, told the NCLAT that copies of the appeal have either not been served on them or that they had not been made parties despite having participated in the proceedings before the NCLT. The NCLAT then asked Chandra to supply copies of the appeal to the appearing parties during the course of the day and take steps to implead the necessary parties. Senior Advocate Dhruv Mehta Chandra has challenged the September 1 order principally on the ground that the Special Principal Bench went beyond the limited scope of a reference arising from a difference of opinion between members of the NCLT. He has also specifically challenged the direction restraining him from alienating “any assets whatsoever either directly or indirectly”. Apart from this restraint, Chandra has objected to the Bench staying the August 25 reasoned opinion of the Third Member and directing fresh replies in pending applications. According to him, these directions effectively reopen the entire proceedings instead of confining the exercise to the specific points on which the original members had differed. Section 419(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with situations where members of an NCLT Bench differ on one or more points. In such a case, the differing members are required to state the point or points of disagreement and refer them to the NCLT President, who may place them before one or more other members. The matter is then decided according to the opinion of the majority of the members who have heard it, including those who originally heard the case. Chandra's case is that this mechanism is meant only to resolve the identified points of difference and cannot be used either to conduct a de novo rehearing of the entire dispute or to impose a sweeping restraint on alienation of his assets. items.title: Festivals not meant for people to die: Bombay High Court moots decibel caps, ban firecrackers on streets
items.summary: Celebrations during festivities are not meant for people to die or suffer, the Bombay High Court orally remarked on Tuesday. A division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale indicated that it will issue an order banning the bursting of firecrackers on public roads across Maharashtra during festivals like Ganeshotsav. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale The sharp remarks came during the hearing of a suo motu case initiated by the Court to address unchecked noise and air pollution caused by high-decibel amplifiers, loud music systems and firecrackers on public streets during festivals. The Court ordered authorities to take immediate preventive action instead of acting on delayed complaints. It directed police to measure noise levels on-site using decibel meters and confiscate equipment violating prescribed norms. “Celebrations are not meant for people to die or suffer health-wise. Nobody would accept this idea that celebrations are there, but at the cost of someone’s health,” the Court said. It also emphasised that celebrations could not happen at the cost of violation of the norms, rules and the tremendous inconvenience to the other citizens . “The excesses have to be controlled,” the judge said. Data submitted during the hearing recorded noise levels reaching up to 106 decibels. While the law permits extended hours until midnight on 15 designated festival days, strict daytime limits up to a maximum of 75 decibels remain mandatory. Advocates noted that those celebrating festivals bypass DJ bans by stacking speakers on pushcarts or beating heavy metal cylinders with hammers. The court criticised the current enforcement mechanism which involves police issuing minor fines of ₹5,000 that effectively act as blanket permissions to break the law. Justice Kulkarni remarked that action must be preventive, failing which damage to thousands of citizens would be already done. “ There is no point. First violating, then going and paying a fine is no good. Filing a criminal complaint, nothing will happen. It has to be preventive. Otherwise, the damage is already done. There is no point in having this kind of mechanism. That is not the correct law and order situation, ” the judge emphasised. items.title: Karnataka MLA Yashavanta Patil resigns over denial of drought-hit status for Indi
items.summary: Karnataka Congress MLA representing Indi constituency, Yashavanta Rayagoud V Patil, resigned from the Legislative Assembly on Wednesday, September 23, in protest over denying his constituency a drought-hit status. Out of the 13 taluks in Vijayapura district, Indi and Chadchan taluks, have been excluded from the state’s list of drought-hit areas. Patil submitted his resignation to Assembly Speaker Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil in Bengaluru. Speaking to reporters, Patil said he was upset with the Karnataka government for failing to declare Indi and Chadchan drought-hit despite repeated appeals. In a letter to Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on August 28, Patil had sought drought-hit status for the two taluks. He had pointed out that 11 of Vijayapura district’s 13 taluks had been declared drought-affected, while Indi and Chadchan were excluded. “I am a ruling party MLA and have made several requests to our government in a sensitive manner so that it does not cause embarrassment. But our words and feelings are not being valued,” Patil wrote. He also alleged that political pressure was influencing whose demands received attention. “In today’s political situation, those who are strong and exert pressure are getting recognition, while people like us, who are mild-natured, are not getting recognition for any work,” he said. Patil said he was unable to do justice to the voters who elected him and was therefore voluntarily resigning as a member of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly. This is the second time Patil has resigned from the Assembly this year. Earlier, he had resigned after being left out of the state Cabinet. He later withdrew his resignation, saying he would continue serving his constituency as an MLA.

items.title: When data mismatch triggers citizenship doubts: SIR and the plight of ordinary voters
items.summary: The ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has produced an unusual situation. Several well-known people including sportsmens, senior politicians, bureaucrats, lawyers, judges have figured in the list of persons issued SIR notices. The reasons mentioned include “Self Name Mismatch”, “Parent Name Mismatch” and “Unmapped with Last SIR”. If persons whose public identity, residence and electoral history are readily verifiable can be flagged because their present electoral particulars do not match or map with a 2002 intensive revision record, it raises a serious question about the limitations of using an old electoral record as the basis for linking or mapping, when that record itself contains many discrepancies and then using it to map the present electoral roll also raises serious concerns. It provides a useful test of the reliability and accuracy of the system. This distinction is important. The question is whether the 2002 database is being used as a tool for verification or whether failure to match with that database is itself being treated as a ground for suspicion about the Citizenship of a voter. These are two very different things. The first is a legitimate verification exercise. The second can become problematic if the system-generated discrepancy is treated as the conclusion rather than as the starting point of an inquiry. The Telangana scenario The Telangana SIR exercise has placed 32,36,659 electors in the category of “unmapped with SIR 2002”, while another 60,50,918 electors have been identified with various anomalies. Together, these two categories cover 92,87,577 electors. The reported discrepancies include differences in names, parent names, relationship types and age details. Such discrepancies may be useful for identifying records that require verification, but they are, at the first stage, only data discrepancies. They are not by themselves evidence of non- citizenship.
